body:
**Bull case**
- FY28 revenue of about ₹1,600 cr at 23% OPM gives PAT of about ₹270 cr (EPS about ₹10.3).
- At 25x that is about ₹258, roughly +29%.
- Multibagger potential needs auto components to reach ₹1,000 cr or more, which is about 2 years away at best.

**Risks**
- Q2 was flattered by one-offs.
- The tariff regime is legally fluid (Section 122 / Section 232 replacement tariffs).
- Freight costs.
- DII distribution.
- Customer concentration in a few global bearing majors.
- The valuation already implies about 17–20% CAGR.

**Kill criteria**
- Q3/Q4 FY27 underlying OPM below 20%.
- Revenue growth below 15% YoY once the refund and pent-up demand fade.
- FY27 auto-component revenue below ₹500 cr.
- DII holding below 22% without FIIs replacing it.

**What would upgrade it:** two more quarters of more than 25% growth at 21% or higher *underlying* OPM, or a pullback to about ₹165–170 (about 20x adjusted).

`theme:sector-metals-mining` · confidence: single-source · tickers: TATASTEEL, JSWSTEEL, JINDALSTEL, SAIL, HINDALCO, VEDL, NMDC, COALINDIA, HINDZINC, NATIONALUM

**How it makes money:** Commodity spread x volume; cost-curve position decides through-cycle returns; miners earn price minus cost with royalty/policy risk.

**Metrics that matter:**
- EBITDA/tonne
- Volume & capacity growth
- Spread over raw materials
- Captive raw material share / cost-curve quartile
- Net debt/EBITDA
- FCF after capex
- Overseas subsidiary losses (Tata Europe)

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Mining (ore, coal, bauxite) -> primary metal (blast furnace/EAF, smelter) -> downstream (coated, rolled, Novelis-type) -> end markets (construction ~60% for steel, auto, capital goods, packaging). Captive mines and downstream value-added products earn the most; non-integrated converters the least.

**Cycle drivers:** China supply/exports, global PMI, domestic infra capex, trade remedies, input coal/ore prices, energy, USD.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- China NBS steel output & exports (monthly)
- SGX iron ore / coking coal futures
- JPC India steel consumption (monthly)
- Indian HRC price trackers (BigMint)
- LME prices & inventories
- DGTR safeguard/anti-dumping notices
- Global manufacturing PMI

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: lowest-cost quartile, captive raw materials, countercyclical capex, deleveraging in upcycles. Losers: overseas acquisitions at peak (2007), leverage into oversupply (2011–16), non-integrated converters.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** EV/EBITDA 4–8x mid-cycle; P/B 0.7x (2015–16, Mar 2020 troughs) to 2–2.5x (2008, 2021 peaks). Low P/E at peak spreads (2021–22) is the classic sell signal.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Q2 FY27: Tata Steel India PAT ₹5,055 cr, India crude steel 6.21 mt (+10%); JSW Steel consolidated PAT ₹5,359 cr, record 7.27 mt crude steel, EBITDA margin ~18.6% vs 15.8%. 12% safeguard duty in place since 2025 (status should be rechecked); CLSA expects stronger H2 FY27.

**Classic traps:**
- Low P/E at peak margin
- Trade-protection-driven pricing that can be withdrawn
- Capacity announcements funded by debt late in cycle
- Miner dividend yield cut by royalty/policy changes

body: `insight:subsidy-and-regulation-margins` · confidence: single-source Several Indian sectors' margins depend on a policy instrument, and the market often capitalises those margins as if they were permanent. EMS: mobile PLI ended in FY26, and Dixon's Q2 FY27 operating margin fell to 2.7% from 3.8%, with ₹1,110 cr of PLI receivables outstanding. Steel: the 12% safeguard duty since 2025 supports domestic spreads. Insurance: the Feb 2023 tax change on high-premium policies cut growth and de-rated insurers, and the Sep 2025 GST exemption removed input tax credit (~60–100 bps of VNB margin). Capital markets: SEBI's F&O curbs (Nov 2024), STT hikes and TER cuts can wipe out 30–50% of a revenue line. Alcobev: one state's excise hike (Maharashtra, 50–60%, June 2025) hits EPS 6–8% for a leader. Pharma: US Section 232 exempted generics only 'at this time' (Apr 2026), with a review due within a year. Renewables: ALMM, customs duty and ISTS-waiver phase-outs change project IRRs. Microfinance: RBI and state lending caps. Checklist: what share of EBITDA comes from incentives, duties or regulated pricing? When does the policy sunset? Who can change it? Has the stock been valued as if the benefit lasts forever? Early signal: management guidance that excludes or quietly normalises incentives, and rising incentive receivables. **lesson:** Haircut policy-dependent margins and value them separately with a sunset date. **examples:** Dixon Q2 FY27 margin drop post-PLI; Maharashtra excise 2025; insurance tax 2023; SEBI F&O 2024; Section 232 review. Sources: [1](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/dixon-q2-income-margin-drop-announcement-cmvv7szk200el2klzhj02h442) · [2](https://www.zeebiz.com/india/news-maharashtra-cabinet-approves-up-to-60-liquor-duty-hike-united-spirits-radico-allied-blenders-stocks-under-pressure-368784) · [3](https://www.india-briefing.com/news/us-patented-pharma-tariff-2026-india-generic-drug-exports-exempted-43899.html) · [4](https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hdfc-life-q1-fy-27-results-net-profit-vnb-july-2026/) Links: about `theme:sector-ems-electronics`, about `theme:sector-alcobev`, about `theme:sector-insurance`, about `theme:sector-amc-capital-markets`, about `insight:sebi-fo-losses`

body:
`person:bill-ackman` | confidence: **verified** | tags: us, process, activism, concentration, blowup

Pershing Square (2004). Structural edge: activist stakes large enough to change boards/management; permanent capital via Pershing Square Holdings (listed 2014) so LPs cannot run. Process: 8-12 simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with pricing power and low leverage, bought when temporarily mispriced, plus cheap asymmetric macro hedges. Signature wins: General Growth Properties after its 2009 bankruptcy (~$60m into ~$1.6bn+, unverified); Canadian Pacific turnaround 2011-16 (~$2.6bn profit, unverified); Chipotle and Hilton; Feb-Mar 2020 credit default swap hedge that made ~$2.6bn (premium cost ~$27m widely reported but not confirmed here). Biggest mistakes: Valeant 2015-17 - concentrated bet on a roll-up whose growth came from price gouging and acquisitions; ~$4bn loss (CNBC). Herbalife $1bn short (2012-18, loss), JC Penney (2010-13, loss). PSH had four straight losing years 2015-18 before +58% (2019) and +70% (2020) (unverified exact figures). Copyable: own a small number of high-quality compounders bought on temporary bad news; use cheap options/hedges where payoff is many times premium; never let a roll-up's adjusted earnings substitute for organic growth (Valeant lesson maps to Indian acquisition-led stories). Not copyable: activism.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| signature_trades | GGP 2009, CP 2011-16, COVID CDS 2020 (+$2.6bn) |
| mistakes | Valeant (-$4bn), Herbalife short, JCPenney |
| copyable | quality concentration on bad news; asymmetric hedges; roll-up skepticism |

title: README › without an LLM: stops after candidates and writes ready-to-paste prompts

body:
- **Cover-letter transcripts:** many banks file only a letter on NSE saying the transcript is on their website.
  `fetch.py` now marks these `cover_letter_only` (not "scanned") and skips them; download the website PDF and pass
  `--local PDF@YYYY-MM-DD` (repeatable, also on `run.py`); it replaces the cover letter for that quarter.
- **Quarter labels:** 7-day lag (banks report in 12–20 days) and a quarter named in the transcript wins.
- **Bank measures** in `score.py`: nim_pct, credit_cost_pct, gnpa_pct, nnpa_pct, slippage_pct, pcr_pct,
  cost_income_pct, cod_pct, cof_pct, yield_advances_pct, casa_ratio_pct, roa_pct, roe_pct, cet1_pct, crar_pct,
  cd_ratio_pct, loan/deposit/casa/fee growth. bps targets are parsed ("40-50 bps" → 0.40–0.50%); ratios use a
  5-bp (tight) or 0.3-pp (wide) tolerance; segment growth and multi-year CAGRs are left to judgment.
  v1 mapped "net interest margin 3.2%" to finance cost (a false miss).
- **`bank_kpis.py`** builds the `--csv` from NSE integrated-filing XBRL (GNPA/NNPA %, CET1, RoA, NII, opex,
  provisions, EPS) plus a `--manual` CSV of deck KPIs (company definitions). Screener's bank page lacks these.
- **Bug fixes (all companies):** "18-20%" was parsed as −20% (dash read as a minus sign); chains now compare the
  ceiling for lower-is-better measures and treat "by FY28" → "at some point" as a goalpost move; a *pending*
  original target is no longer pre-judged moved-goalpost (flag `goalpost_flag`, resolve at its deadline). On the
  19-Nov pilot seeds: SKIPPER auto moved-goalposts 12 → 9 and restatements 4 → 7, statuses otherwise unchanged;
  UNIPARTS unchanged.
- Candour heuristic no longer treats "slippage(s)" as an admission; bank categories added to the LLM prompt.
